chapters.title: The boy at the window
chapters.subtitle: The lesson was inside. My attention was elsewhere.
paragraphs: The world has never had much difficulty getting my attention. A bird beyond a window, a scrap of music, the possibility of a game—any one of them could loosen the hold of a classroom. There was always something happening just outside the lesson.

I was a mischievous child in a pious family. Perhaps that is as good a beginning as any: reverence and restlessness under the same roof. The adults had their ideas about the proper direction of a life. I had an eye on the window.

Music offered one kind of freedom; sport offered another. One invited me to listen, the other to move. Both asked for an attention I could give without being persuaded. Curiosity, when left to itself, has a remarkable appetite.

Beyond the classroom were birds, trees, and the open sky. It would be too tidy to turn every wandering glance into a revelation. Sometimes a boy is simply distracted. Sometimes the distraction is the part he remembers.
Looking back, I am drawn to that window as a place to begin. On one side, the world being explained. On the other, the world inviting me to come and see.

chapters.title: Roots and restlessness
chapters.subtitle: What we inherit. What we make our own.
paragraphs: We arrive in the middle of a story. Before we have a name for ourselves, there are names behind us, ways of looking at the world, and ideas about what a life ought to become. An inheritance can be felt long before it is understood.

Mine was a spiritual inheritance. My ancestors were yogis; piety belonged to the family into which I was born. But an inheritance is only the beginning of the conversation. Each life must find its own way of answering.

My temperament added a little mischief to the question. I was drawn to experience, to movement, to whatever lay around the next corner. The world seemed full of invitations, and I was rarely inclined to leave them unopened.
Must we resemble our roots in every visible way? A tree does not grow by returning to the earth. It reaches outward, becoming something its roots make possible but cannot entirely predict.
That is the space this story inhabits: affection for what came before, and curiosity about what might come next. The old questions remain. The life that asks them is my own.

chapters.title: The art of being both
chapters.subtitle: A little stillness. A little appetite. A whole life.
paragraphs: There is a part of me that wants to sit quietly with the great questions. There is another that would like to know what is happening outside. They have been sharing a life for some time now.

The yogi and the bhogi make interesting companions. One listens for what lies beneath the noise; the other finds the music in it. One turns inward. The other opens a window. Between them is the possibility of a life large enough to contain more than a single answer.
I am interested in that meeting place. In the pleasure that makes us more attentive. In the pause that allows an experience to settle. In the moment when curiosity becomes a question worth carrying.

Balance sounds like a still thing until you try to live it. Then it becomes movement: leaning, noticing, returning. A little more patience here; a little more courage there. The work is in the adjustment.
These pages follow that movement. There will be room for delight and doubt, for mischief and reflection, for the ways a life escapes the neat description prepared for it. For now, the window is open.
